brief: Scotiabank recaps the October 28 FOMC meeting: the Committee held the funds rate at 3.75%-4% as expected, voting 10-2, with Governors Cook and Hammack dissenting for a 25bp hike; two previously hawkish members (Kashkari, Logan) did not dissent this time. The statement upgraded growth language to 'strong' from 'solid' and added a line on gathering more information before setting policy, which markets read as slightly dovish. Author Derek Holt argues the Fed skipped a hike mainly to avoid violating its dot plot, since a surprise move would have pushed markets to price a December hike and created tension before hawkish voters lose their votes in the new year; OIS pricing for December 9 was trimmed only 1-2bp and still favors a hike, which Scotia expects. Warsh announced fewer policy meetings from 2027 (one of eight becomes strategy-only) and six decision meetings in 2028. Balance sheet plans begin unveiling from Q1, and five task forces target year-end reports, though not all will meet it; the productivity and jobs group holds a public hearing November 16.

cards.claim: The FOMC left the federal funds target range unchanged at 3.75%-4% at the October 28, 2026 meeting, as widely expected.
cards.anchor: The Committee left the fed funds target range unchanged at 3.75% – 4% as widely expected and priced.

cards.claim: Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissented from the October decision, preferring to raise the target range by 25 basis points.
cards.anchor: Lisa D. Cook and Beth M. Hammack, who preferred to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point

cards.claim: Minneapolis Fed President Kashkari and Dallas Fed President Logan, previously among the most hawkish FOMC members, did not dissent at the October meeting.
cards.anchor: two of the previously most hawkish members did not dissent this time (Minneapolis President Kashkari and Dallas President Logan)

cards.claim: The FOMC's October statement upgraded its description of economic activity to a 'strong' pace from 'solid pace' in September.
cards.anchor: They upgraded reference to the economy’s performance to a “strong” pace from “solid pace.”

cards.claim: The FOMC's October statement added language saying the accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the appropriate policy stance.
cards.anchor: The accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation

cards.claim: Markets interpreted the FOMC's October communications as slightly dovish.
cards.anchor: Markets took the communications as slightly dovish

cards.claim: Scotiabank's Derek Holt argues the main reason the Fed skipped a hike in October was that a surprise hike would have violated its own dot plot.
cards.anchor: the main argument for skipping today was that a surprise hike would violate the dots

cards.claim: OIS pricing for the Fed's December 9 meeting was trimmed by only 1-2 basis points after the October decision and still leans heavily toward a hike.
cards.anchor: OIS pricing for the December 9th meeting was very slightly trimmed by 1–2bps but still leans heavily toward a hike at that meeting

cards.claim: Scotiabank expects the Fed to hike rates at the December 9 FOMC meeting.
cards.anchor: still leans heavily toward a hike at that meeting which we expect

cards.claim: The Fed's balance sheet task force conclusions will likely feed into the FOMC early in the first quarter, though Chair Warsh cautioned the timing is not firm.
cards.anchor: Their conclusions will be fed into the FOMC probably early in the first quarter but don't hold me to that timing

cards.claim: The Fed will keep eight meetings in 2027, but one of them will be a strategy-focused meeting with no statement or policy vote.
cards.anchor: The present eight meetings per year schedule would be maintained in 2027, but one would focus upon broad policy strategy with neither a statement

cards.claim: In 2028, the Fed will hold six decision meetings and two strategy meetings per year.
cards.anchor: In 2028, there would be six decision-meetings and two strategy meetings.

cards.claim: Chair Warsh said most but not all of the Fed's five task forces will meet their year-end reporting deadline.
cards.anchor: I gave them a year-end deadline. Some but not all of the groups will hit the deadline.

cards.claim: The Fed's productivity and jobs task force will hold a public field hearing on November 16 lasting three to four hours.
cards.anchor: On November 16th the productivity and jobs task force will do a field hearing inviting a broad range of people.

cards.claim: Chair Warsh said AI-driven capital expenditure is broadening beyond just strength in the technology sector.
cards.anchor: the cap-ex story is not just strong, it is broadening.

cards.claim: Chair Warsh said that since September, rate-driven differentiation among investments has widened credit spreads.
cards.anchor: Market participants are discriminating between investments, spreads have widened out.

cards.claim: Chair Warsh said the Fed's 2% inflation target is measured by PCE and that it took six years for inflation to reach the level referenced in the question.
cards.anchor: There is a 2% target measured by PCE. It took six years for inflation to have the effect your reference.

cards.claim: Chair Warsh said the historically stable correlation between oil prices and interest rates has weakened, with energy prices rising while rates rolled over to the downside.
cards.anchor: Energy prices have gone up but interest rates have rolled over to the downside.

cards.claim: Chair Warsh said oil futures prices have moved up over the last several weeks.
cards.anchor: futures prices have moved up over the last several weeks

cards.claim: Scotiabank's Derek Holt contrasts Fed Chair Warsh's backward-looking communication style with Bank of Canada Governor Macklem's forward-looking, forecast-driven approach.
cards.anchor: Warsh remains very backward looking with his assessments, whereas Macklem is all about forecasts.

cards.claim: Chair Warsh said financial conditions have tightened, which may have partly explained the FOMC's uneventful October communications.
cards.anchor: financial conditions have tightened and that may have been a partial reason for the fairly uneventful communications
